transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir (AE, Redwood); Priya (SE, Redwood); Diego (CSM, Redwood); Alex (CTO, Lynx); Marta (Head infra, Lynx); Ben (SRE, Lynx); Jia (PM, Lynx)

[00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — happy Monday. Quick roll call, we have Alex, Marta, Ben, Jia from Lynx, and Priya and Diego from Redwood. How's everyone?
[00:12] Alex (Lynx): Good, thanks Samir. Trying to keep this short, we've got a Friday exec review next week so want to make sure renewal options and the EU burst are nailed down.
[00:20] Samir: Great. Agenda: renewal term/pricing, burst vs reserved capacity sizing, VPC onboarding for PII work, and a quick perf target check for your EU traffic. If anything else just shout.
[00:34] Marta (Lynx): Sounds good. We'll also want to re-confirm audit log retention and key management—some folks in compliance will ask.
[00:41] Priya (SE): Totally, we'll cover SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration steps.

-- Discovery / Context --
[01:05] Samir: Alex, can you remind us where you landed on hosted vs dedicated? My notes say you were leaning dedicated with VPC for the sensitive pipelines, but still use hosted for lower-sensitivity features. Is that still right?
[01:18] Alex: Yeah that's right. For customer PII pipelines we want VPC + dedicated capacity, ideally pinned to a model family with predictable latency. For experiments and new features, we can keep hitting the hosted API. Cost is a factor, though — dedicated commitments need to prove unit economics.
[01:34] Ben (Lynx): Also, latency — we need 95th percentile under 200ms for short requests (<=128 tokens) from EU. For longer gen jobs we accept bursts but need consistent throughput.
[01:47] Priya: That's helpful. Our Dedicated pools with EU region nodes usually hit those numbers when model selection and batching are tuned; depends on tokenization and kv cache usage. We can demo exact numbers with your sample trace.

-- Renewal sizing discussion --
[03:12] Samir: For the renewal we put together three packages: conservative (current commit), growth (x2 core tokens/day, includes burst buckets), and aggressive (x3 with reserved nodes). Marta — which looks closest to your forecast?
[03:26] Marta: Probably the growth plan but we'd want the burst to be usable for black-Friday-like peaks — not daily. How does Redwood throttle burst to ensure reserved customers don't get bumped?
[03:36] Diego (CSM): We expose a burst policy — you can set burst pool size, cooldown windows, and preemption rules. For Dedicated customers we can guarantee baseline throughput; bursts draw from shared spare capacity but we can provide an elevated SLA during agreed windows.
[03:49] Alex: If we agree on a 12-month renewal, what's the uplift on pricing per token for reserved vs burst? I want a sense of delta.
[03:56] Samir: I'll share a pricing matrix after the call. Roughly speaking reserved capacity lowers per-token costs by ~20-30% compared to on-demand, burst usage priced slightly higher than reserved but still below fully on-demand hosted in most cases — I'll send concrete numbers.

-- Technical deep dive (SE-led) --
[05:12] Priya: On the VPC onboarding: the Private control plane will still manage deployments but data egress happens through your VPC peering or a customer-managed NAT — you keep the keys. KMS/HSM integration is supported; we have a short checklist.
[05:29] Ben: Do you support our internal KMS provider? We run Vault with HSM-backed keys.
[05:33] Priya: Yep, we have a Vault integration pattern, we probably need a few config items and an in-place token rotation cadence. Diego will share the doc.
[05:40] Marta: Audit logs — retention options? We need 13 months for some regs.
[05:44] Diego: We can extend audit retention as an add-on. Default is 90 days, but enterprise customers often pick 12–24 months. We'll include the SOC2 summary and log retention options in the packet.

-- Performance targets & benchmarking --
[07:05] Priya: For the EU 95th <200ms goal — we should run a replay with sample traffic at your desired concurrency. For short 64–128 token calls, the kernel and quantization profile matter. Do you have an example sample?
[07:18] Alex: Yes, Ben has a replay artifact. Ben, can you upload it to the share?
[07:21] Ben: I'll drop the S3 link after this call. It's about 2.5M token/day profile.
[07:26] Priya: Perfect. We'll run a 1-hour bench: measure p95, mean, and tail for both hosted EU and Dedicated EU nodes. We'll also run with and without KV cache hot-warm scenario.
[07:36] Jia: Timeline — how long to get a VPC sandbox up? We have to show infra team a runbook.
[07:41] Priya: For a sandbox, usually 7–10 business days after we get the network peering details and firewall exceptions. Full production rollouts with vault/KMS and longer retention could take 3–6 weeks depending on your approvals.
[07:52] Marta: That's okay. The execs want a go/no-go by 3/19 to align budgets.
[07:56] Samir: So we need the sample replay and decision-makers list by 3/11 to hit that target.

-- Objections and tradeoffs --
[09:10] Alex: Biggest risk is unit cost at scale — if we commit and usage doesn't ramp, it's risky. Can we do ramped commitments or credits for unused tokens?
[09:21] Samir: We can do staged commitments — example: 6 months at X baseline then step-up. For unused tokens we typically don't credit beyond negotiated annual true-ups, but I can propose a capped roll-over for year one.
[09:33] Diego: Also we can include a pilot period where you get a lower-commitment trial for Dedicated nodes for a defined window to validate perf before full commit.
[09:41] Marta: That pilot option could help. What's the minimum pilot size?
[09:44] Priya: We can provision a small dedicated pool (2-4 cards) to validate latency. Depends which model family you pick — smaller Llama-like family runs cheaper.

-- Security and compliance specifics --
[11:05] Ben: For the SOC2 docs — do you provide the control matrix mapping to our policies?
[11:10] Diego: Yes, we have a SOC2 control matrix and an ISO snapshot; I'll attach redacted versions. Also the VPC checklist spells out which logs are customer-owned vs Redwood-managed.
[11:20] Alex: SSO/SAML? We need role-based access for our infra and product folks.
[11:24] Priya: Supported — SAML/SCIM + RBAC. We can demo admin flows in the console; Diego can include a short video link.

-- Pricing nuance conversation --
[13:00] Jia: On pricing, can we get per-route token cap to prevent runaway costs in experiments?
[13:06] Samir: Yes, per-route rate limits and token caps are configurable in the console. We'll include recommended guardrails in the proposal.

-- Recap and agreement --
[20:12] Samir: Quick recap: Lynx will share sample replay and stakeholder list by 3/11; Redwood will run the bench and share results by 3/12; Samir will send renewal pricing scenarios by 3/09; Diego to send VPC checklist and SOC2 artifacts by 3/10. Pilot dedicated pool option on table.
[20:45] Alex: Looks right. Also want the suggested rollback/fallback plan documented — if Dedicated saturates we need automatic fallback to hosted with preserved auth and logs.
[20:55] Priya: We have an automated routing policy that can fallback to a compatible model variant on hosted — there will be a note on logging continuity. We'll include the flow in the runbook.

-- Closing --
[22:15] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the benchmark. If anything urgent, ping me.
[22:22] Alex: Appreciate it.
[22:26] Marta: Thanks.
